verdict.rationale: Pipecat ships an official CLI (pypi pipecat-ai[cli]) with documented subcommands. They include `init` for scaffolding, which also writes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, `cloud` for deployment, `eval` for behavioral evals, and `context-hub install`, which registers an MCP server and local index for coding agents. A runtime probe confirms `pipecat --help` runs keylessly and lists these commands. missing for 10: independent community or hands-on corroboration beyond the vendor docs and probe, and deeper documentation of each CLI subcommand's options.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: the official Pipecat CLI (pypi pipecat-ai[cli]) ran keylessly via uvx — `pipecat --help` lists init (project scaffolding), cloud (deploy to Pipecat Cloud), eval (behavioral evals), and context-hub (local docs/examples/API index built for coding agents).
Install the Pipecat CLI and scaffold the quickstart project (also writes AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md)
pipecat context-hub install registers the hub as an MCP server with your coding agent and builds the local index
